body:
Pip, good news: two changes to speed things up. YY approved both in the project thread at 2026-10-15T19:28:33Z ("yes please"), in answer to my question "Should I loosen the retry rule and tell Pip to start the next issues in parallel?". No science, refusal, data, migration or production rule changes.

**1. One re-run after a harmless glitch (build and proof tooling reviewed from now on)**

A tooling graph may declare one re-run root next to its first root, for example the first root plus `-rerun1`. The re-run uses the same exact bytes, bindings and guards. My Source review covers both runs, and you may use the re-run once without a new review when all of these hold:
- The first run stopped on an environment glitch in a measurement, bookkeeping, network or download step, not in the app's own work and not in a guard. The 180000 du ENOENT is the model case.
- Nothing was cleaned, pruned, deployed, or written to a production database or volume.
- The first run's evidence is closed and published (raw bytes plus hashes) before the re-run starts.
- Fresh R4, unused-root and unit checks pass for the re-run root.

These still need a new review:
- any guard or binding refusal;
- any hash, integrity, FK, science or refusal-check failure;
- an R4 shortfall;
- unexplained growth over 500 MB;
- a memory or time limit hit by the app's own work, such as the 600 s READY limit;
- any second failure.

Production releases (quiesce, backup, install, deploy) stay forward-only with no re-run.

The current 190000 graph (4de3e334) has a single fixed root. If it trips on a glitch, send a resubmission that changes only the root name and the closed-failure reference. I'll review just that diff, not the whole graph.

**2. Start the remaining issues now, in parallel**

Still open: #203, #204, #207, #208, #215, #216, #217. Their prerequisites are already on main (be837974 includes #206, #214 and #209), so branch from current main.

Suggested order (you can adjust):
1. #208 labels and #207 storage, the lab-facing follow-ups to #206.
2. #216 LOD/LOQ and #215 QA dashboard.
3. #203 and #204, the bench polish.
4. #217 last, since the cleanup touches everything.

The usual gate applies: one PR per issue, the `ready-for-audit` label, and my verdict on the exact head.

One hold: please don't merge anything into main until the be837974 release is deployed and post-deploy checked. The build and proof tooling refuses if main moves, so audits can go ahead now and merges queue until then. Migrations stay additive only, and there's still no hard-coded lab policy.
